question: Whether ordinary Skill activation/retrigger callers consume distinct rejection causes or only success/failure, and whether failure continuations actually exist.
scope: Selected ordinary native Skill, Character, SkillState and UI branches; no client execution or active XLua validation; no exhaustive all-character claim.

confirmed.fact: BasicSkill.Cast returns bool. Failed IsAvailable returns false directly; failed DoCast dispatches each Behaviour.OnCastFailed with no parameters and then returns false. Successful DoCast invokes OnCastSucceed and returns true.
confirmed.slotEvidence: BasicSkill.IsAvailable slot 19; DoCast slot 52; OnCastSucceed slot 65. Behaviour.OnCastFailed slot 7, called through class offset 0x1b0.

confirmed.fact: CastSkill.DoCast and CastSkillWithCost.DoCast both return bool. Ordinary CastSkill tests Ability cast success before ReduceSp. WithCost tests ReduceSp success before attempting the Ability. The upstream BasicSkill.Cast consumes only the returned bool; neither result carries a rejection-cause payload.

Character.OpTrigSkill selects ordinary trigger or retrigger, checks the corresponding bool eligibility and bool execution result, logs a successful operation, and returns true; failures merge into false. It does not branch on SP/control/target rejection codes.

RetriggerableCastSkillWithCost.RetriggerSkill tests bool eligibility. Its deferred path sets a pending flag, tests UseSkill's bool, and clears the flag on failure. Direct _DoRetrigger returns bool; a failed ReduceCost exits false. No distinct rejection-cause result is consumed in these selected paths.

SkillState has a separate failure path: canUseAbility=false and non-uninterruptible Skill calls OnCastFailedInSkillState. That void callback has no parameters and dispatches the same no-argument Behaviour.OnCastFailed. It is not a returned reason code from BasicSkill.Cast.
confirmed.slotEvidence: SkillState tests BasicSkill.get_stateUninterruptible slot 17 and calls OnCastFailedInSkillState slot 66.

confirmed.fact: The menu button calls BattleController.PlayerOp_TrigSkill and proceeds to tutorial/UI state work without inspecting a Skill rejection cause.

Failure continuations exist and must not be conflated with no-op rejection: OxiFireRainSlotBehaviour.OnCastFailed checks current Ability.isCasting and Skill.isAffecting, then may call _Leave. FeverBehaviour.OnCastFailed conditionally calls _LeaveFeverIfNecessary. Both callbacks take no cause argument; selected decisions read current domain facts.
confirmed.limitation: Native implementation exists; this sub-investigation does not prove a current actual character binding for these two Behaviours.

contentEvidence.priorBinding: Archived catap2 S1 uses CastSkillWithCost; S2 uses RetriggerableCastSkillWithCost, with concrete first-payment/start-effect flow.
contentEvidence.currentStatus: Current skills.ab and buff template bundle hashes differ; archived MonoScript source file is absent. The historical binding is not relabelled as a current content proof; individual verification outcomes are in content-reuse.json.

conclusion: Selected real Skill calling protocols require success/failure and contain distinct failure continuations, but none of the covered callers consumes a structured SP/control/no-target rejection cause. This does not prove such a requirement absent from all game content. No ArkBattle API design decision is made here.
